content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm using a [product_name] version [version_no] ([article_no]) and tried using an SD card, but it's not detected by the device. My SD card is 32 GB, formatted with FAT32 and a 64 KB allocation unit size. Interestingly, the same SD card works flawlessly with the previous [product_name] version [version_no] ([article_no]). I've tried formatting both with and without Quick Format using Windows, and after multiple attempts, the SD card eventually worked. I'd like to understand why the SD card only works with [product_name] [version_no] and not [version_no], and if there are any specific requirements or recommendations for using SD cards with these devices. Thank you in advance.
For [product_name] [version_no], you can also try formatting the SD card with exFAT.
I've already tried exFAT formatting but it still doesn't work.

I'm unable to assist further; maybe another user has a solution. I own several [product_name] devices and have tested many SD cards with different brands, classes, and capacities. I have not encountered any problems—all my cards are FAT32 formatted. Capacity issues only occur with cards larger than 64 GB, for which I create a 32 GB FAT32 partition, and they also work fine.
Delete all existing partitions on the SD card, then create a new FAT32 partition. You can use third-party software like MiniTool Partition Wizard Free for this task.

Hi, do you consider yourself fortunate to have a working [product_name]? I purchased a [product_name] without a display and couldn't get any SD card to work, despite trying several brands, capacities, and both exFAT and FAT32. The card was never recognized. I returned the device, since I couldn't start the web server without an SD card. In contrast, a 64G card worked fine in a previous [product_name]. It would be helpful if [company_name] provided better guidance on SD card compatibility in the manuals and recommended specific manufacturers, sizes, and formats for reliable operation. Best regards, [user_name]
Hi, why do you want to delete partitions? A full (non-quick) format will remove them all. Best regards, [user_name]

As I mentioned, I've tried various SD cards from different brands and capacities and haven't experienced any issues. I don't see the need for [company_name] to specify manufacturers; the specifications in the manual are sufficient.
No, that's not correct. You should learn more about partitioning and start sectors.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are having mixed experiences with SD card compatibility on [product_name] [version_no] units. Some users can use a wide range of SD cards without issue, while others face persistent incompatibility, preventing essential features like the web server from working. There are requests for clearer guidelines and manufacturer recommendations in official documentation to help ensure reliable SD card operation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect SD card compatibility to be uniform across different device versions, with specific, reliable guidance for choosing and setting up supported cards. They're looking for clear troubleshooting advice for getting SD cards to work with [product_name] [version_no].
